c076.front: How does a system privilege differ from an object privilege?
c076.back: A system privilege lets you perform a kind of action, for example CREATE TABLE or CREATE SESSION. An object privilege applies to one specific object, for example SELECT ON t. An easy test: an object privilege always has ON.

c077.front: WITH GRANT OPTION vs WITH ADMIN OPTION: how do they differ?
c077.back: WITH GRANT OPTION is for object privileges. When you revoke it, it also disappears from people someone passed it on to (cascade). WITH ADMIN OPTION is for system privileges and roles. Here a revoke does not cascade: the others keep it.

c078.front: Can an object privilege be granted on selected columns only?
c078.back: Yes, but only INSERT, UPDATE and REFERENCES, for example GRANT UPDATE (salary) ON emp TO u. SELECT on columns is not possible. Create a view with the chosen columns and grant SELECT on the view.

c079.front: Which privilege lets a user log in?
c079.back: CREATE SESSION. Without it the login fails (ORA-01045).
c079.try_sql:
-- Without CREATE SESSION you could not log in and run this query
SELECT privilege FROM session_privs WHERE privilege = 'CREATE SESSION';

c080.front: Is a role a schema object?
c080.back: No. A role belongs to no schema. A role can be granted to another role, and it can be granted to PUBLIC.
c080.try_sql:
-- The EMPLOYEES table is a schema object, the CONNECT and RESOURCE roles are not: they are not in ALL_OBJECTS
SELECT owner, object_name, object_type FROM all_objects WHERE object_name IN ('EMPLOYEES', 'CONNECT', 'RESOURCE');

c700.front: Can you revoke UPDATE from just one column?
c700.back: No, you get ORA-01750. UPDATE/REFERENCES can be granted on columns, but must be revoked from the whole table: REVOKE UPDATE ON t FROM u.

c701.front: Which object privileges can be granted on a sequence, and which on a view?
c701.back: A sequence: only SELECT and ALTER (others raise ORA-02205). A view: SELECT and the DML privileges (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE…), but not ALTER, INDEX or EXECUTE (ORA-02204).

c702.front: How does SESSION_PRIVS differ from USER_SYS_PRIVS?
c702.back: SESSION_PRIVS shows the system privileges you can use now, in this session, including those from enabled roles. USER_SYS_PRIVS shows only the system privileges granted to you directly, with the ADMIN_OPTION column.

c703.front: When does a grant take effect for a user who is already logged in?
c703.back: System and object privileges take effect at once. A new role works only after SET ROLE or in a new session (after logging in again).

c704.front: Can WITH GRANT OPTION be given to a role? And to PUBLIC?
c704.back: Not to a role: you get ORA-01926. To a user or to PUBLIC: yes.

c705.front: What happens to the granted privileges when you drop the table?
c705.back: They disappear with the table. If you then create a new table with the same name, it has no grants at all.

c1700.front: GRANT SELECT on a synonym: what is recorded?
c1700.back: A grant on the object the synonym points to. In USER_TAB_PRIVS_MADE you see the table, not the synonym. A synonym is only a second name.

c1701.front: GRANT ... TO a user that does not exist: what happens?
c1701.back: Error ORA-01917: user or role does not exist. Oracle does not remember grants "for the future". Only a grant to PUBLIC also covers users created later.

c1702.front: REVOKE ALL when you granted only some privileges?
c1702.back: It works and takes away what you really granted. But if you name a privilege you never granted (for example REVOKE SELECT, INSERT ...), you get ORA-01927 and nothing is revoked.

c1703.front: ORA-00942 or ORA-01031 on another user's table: when is which?
c1703.back: ORA-00942: you have no privilege at all, so the table looks as if it did not exist. ORA-01031: you can see the table (for example you have SELECT), but you lack this particular privilege, for example UPDATE. 23ai gives the more precise ORA-41900 (missing UPDATE privilege) instead.

c1704.front: You want to grant SELECT on your view that reads another user's table. What do you need?
c1704.back: You must have SELECT on that other table WITH GRANT OPTION. Without it, the GRANT fails with ORA-01720.

c1705.front: You create a view on A.T, but you have SELECT on A.T only through a role. What happens?
c1705.back: Error ORA-01031. Objects stored in the database (views, procedures) do not use privileges from roles. A direct grant is needed.

c1706.front: Cascade on REVOKE: A→B (with grant option)→C, and also A→C directly. A revokes the privilege from B. What next?
c1706.back: B loses the privilege, and the grants made by B disappear. But C keeps access, because C also got it directly from A.

c1707.front: REVOKE REFERENCES when someone has a foreign key based on that privilege?
c1707.back: Error ORA-01981, unless you add CASCADE CONSTRAINTS. Then the dependent foreign keys are dropped.

c1708.front: What do the CONNECT and RESOURCE roles give?
c1708.back: CONNECT gives CREATE SESSION, that is, logging in. RESOURCE gives CREATE TABLE, SEQUENCE, PROCEDURE, TRIGGER, TYPE…, but not CREATE SESSION. So RESOURCE alone is not enough to log in.

c1709.front: You have a role without ADMIN OPTION. Can you grant it to someone else?
c1709.back: No: error ORA-01932. You need that role WITH ADMIN OPTION, or the GRANT ANY ROLE privilege.

c1710.front: Schema privileges in 23ai: what are they?
c1710.back: For example GRANT SELECT ANY TABLE ON SCHEMA hr TO u. It is an ANY privilege, but for one schema only. It also covers tables created later. You see them in USER_SCHEMA_PRIVS. 19c does not have this syntax.
c1710.try_sql:
-- Schema privileges granted to you (23ai); 19c does not have this view
SELECT * FROM user_schema_privs;

c1711.back: A ready-made role for a developer. It contains, among others, CREATE SESSION, CREATE DOMAIN, CREATE JOB… and the RESOURCE role. It contains no ANY privileges. Your practice schema does not have this role: it gets selected CREATE privileges directly.
c1711.try_sql:
-- Your privileges in the session (you do not have DB_DEVELOPER_ROLE, only a few CREATE privileges granted directly)
SELECT privilege FROM session_privs ORDER BY privilege;
